audit.whatIsWrong: The chart gave Kayle levels 2 and 3 while whys[1] and whys[2] say 'concede this level entirely' and 'Still his'. It also called levels 4-5 and level 6 skill lanes while the prose and packet both give them to Kayle. On top of that, whys[3] and whys[4] were swapped: the level-6 explanation sat on the levels 4-5 row and the 4-5 explanation sat on the level-6 row.
audit.why: Graves' Quickdraw dash into True Grit-stacked shotgun autos beats a melee Kayle outright at 2-3; from 6 on she is ranged with an invulnerability button and he plateaus as a tanky ADC.
audit.corrected: Rows 1-4 flipped as one atomic group to Graves, Graves, Kayle, Kayle — matching the packet and the Graves-side audit — with the swapped whys re-seated on the right rows and all four phases[].why lines rewritten.

audit.whatIsWrong: Neither the level-6 phase nor the do's carried a cooldown number for the two abilities the whole page is built around.
audit.why: Divine Judgment is 160s at rank 1 — you get one per lane phase, so it must be spent on his commit. Quickdraw is 16s at rank 1 and refunds off his basic attacks, which is why 'when it's down' is a narrow window, not a standing state.
audit.corrected: 160s at rank 1 in phases[4].why and whys[4]; Quickdraw's 16s and its auto-attack refund in dosFull[0].d and phases[3].why.
sources: enemyKit E cd 16/15/14/13/12 and refund text

audit.whatIsWrong: The page said Smoke Screen 'blinds' your autos and that your DPS 'drops to zero' inside it. Riot's text says it creates a cloud that reduces sight range, damages and briefly slows on impact — there is no blind and no attack-miss.
audit.why: A player told their autos miss will walk out of a fight they were winning. The Graves-side audit already corrected this in the same direction.
audit.corrected: whys[2], early and wants.foe[1] now describe the sight cut and the impact slow. Also added the End of the Line retreat cut-off with the Flash note, which nothing on the page carried.

audit.why: packet.suspectNames flagged "Starfire Spellblade's" in spikes[2]; that is Kayle's real E name, so it is a false positive.
sources: ownerKit E text naming Virtue/Starfire Spellblade

edits.before: Levels 1-3 are entirely his. You are melee-range with only Q (Radiant Blast) and one point of W, and Graves' shotgun cone plus his Quickdraw dash let him close, dump True Grit-fueled autos, and reset before you can answer. Do not contest the wave or trade your Q into his burst — last-hit at max range, eat a little CS loss, and respect that his level 2-3 all-in can flat kill you. If he drops Smoke Screen on you, walk out of the cloud before you waste autos into the blind.
edits.after: Levels 1-3 are entirely his. You are melee-range with only Q (Radiant Blast) and one point of W, and Graves' shotgun cone plus his Quickdraw dash let him close, dump True Grit-fueled autos, and reset before you can answer. Do not contest the wave or trade your Q into his burst — last-hit at max range, eat a little CS loss, and respect that his level 2-3 all-in can flat kill you. If he drops Smoke Screen on you, walk out of the cloud: it cuts your sight and slows, it does not blind.

notes: Two real defects here beyond the chart: whys[3] and whys[4] were written for each other's rows, and the page claimed Smoke Screen blinds. Riot's text is a sight-range cut with an impact slow and brief slow — no blind, no attack-miss — so every line depending on it was rewritten. Rows 1-4 flipped as one atomic group in both layers to match the packet and the Graves-side audit. The kit's derived 'terrain' flag on End of the Line contradicts Riot's description (it detonates on terrain, it does not create it); I wrote only what the description supports, matching the Graves-side note.
